newsitem.title: UK: EIU expects Eastern European growth to slow.
newsitem.headline: EIU expects Eastern European growth to slow.

text.p: Economic growth in Eastern Europe, excluding the former USSR, is expected to deteriorate in 1997, with average 1997 gross domestic product (GDP) growth slowing to 3.2 percent from 3.7 percent in 1996, the Economist Intelligience Unit (EIU) said in a report received on Thursday.
"The need to deal with balance of payments problems will have a marked impact on Czech and Slovak performance," said Laza Kekic, EIU director of transition economies.

Poland and Hungary are expected to resist spillover effects of the Czech crisis, but Kekic said a further slowdown for the Balkan economies is expected because of continuing political turmoil and austerity policies.
But in its latest review, the EIU said improving performance in most of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) and the Baltic states means average growth in the transition region will turn up.

"The expected bottoming out of the Russian recession, in addition to the strong recovery in many Central Asian and Transcaucasian state, will mean growth in the transition region as a whole will turn positive in 1997 for the first time since the beginning of reform," it said.
The EIU expected growth for Eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union of 1.4 percent compared with a 1.4-percent decline in 1996.
According to the report, 1997 total foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows are projected at $14.5 billion, below the record $16 billion in 1995.
